newsitem.title: USA: First Enterprise Q4 charge-offs $2.7 mln.
newsitem.headline: First Enterprise Q4 charge-offs $2.7 mln.

text.p: First Enterprise Financial Group Inc said fourth-quarter charge-offs to loss reserves were $2.7 million, $1.1 million of which were unanticipated.
"Because of the additional provision, the company eliminated all 1996 management bonuses, which would have totaled approximately $750,000," the company said.

The used auto loans company said its financial condition is sound and it is in compliance with covenants contained in its debt instruments. It said it is confident that "current analysts' estimates of 1997 earnings can be achieved."
"In view of recent industry experience, the company took a hard look at its receivable portfolio, resulting in the additional fourth quarter charge-offs," said chief executive Michael Harrington.

"Management has reemphasized sound credit and collection procedures. The company continues to seek a conservative position in its loss reserves and believes the increase in loss reserves is appropriate," he said.
The allowance for credit losses at December 31 was 9.6 percent of the average net portfolio versus 8.4 percent at December 31, 1995, the company said.

Accounts delinquent 60 days or more were 1.7 percent of the total owned and serviced portfolio at December 31, compared with 1.1 percent at December 31, 1995. Net charge-offs for the total portfolio were 7.4 percent in 1996, versus 6.5 percent in 1995, First Enterprise said.
